what.question: What is Mochi?
what.answer: Mochi is a period tracker app for iPhone with a cute mascot. It predicts your next period, reminds you when to change your pad and rewards daily check-ins with 12 collectible flavors.

free.question: Is Mochi free?
free.answer: Yes. Cycle tracking, predictions, the pad change reminder, moods, streaks and starter flavors are free. Mochi Plus is optional.

private.question: Is my period data private?
private.answer: Yes. Period dates, flow, symptoms and moods stay on your iPhone by default, unless you enable optional backup. They are never sent to analytics, logs or crash reports. Our privacy policy explains how optional backup works.

offline.question: Does Mochi work without an account or internet?
offline.answer: Yes. Every core feature works offline and no account is required. An account is optional if you want backup and sync.

reminder.question: How does the pad change reminder work?
reminder.answer: Choose a day pad, overnight pad or liner and a duration from 2 to 8 hours. Mochi counts down on Home, in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen.

lockScreen.question: Will my Lock Screen show that I'm on my period?
lockScreen.answer: No. The Live Activity uses private, discreet wording and never states that you are on your period.

medical.question: Can I use Mochi as birth control?
medical.answer: No. Mochi's predictions are estimates for period awareness, not contraception, diagnosis or medical advice.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: Mochi collects only the information you choose to add in the app, such as your period dates, flow, symptoms, moods, sex, tests and pregnancy logs. This data is used to give you cycle predictions, reminders and a personalized experience (like your streaks and collectible flavors).
collect.detail: We do not collect or require your name, email or any other personal information to use the app. You can enjoy all core features without creating an account.

device.title: What stays on your iPhone
device.body: Your cycle data lives in a local database on your iPhone. It’s used only by Mochi to show your cycle, make predictions and keep your streaks and flavors.
device.detail: You stay in control. Your data is not sent to analytics, logs or crash reports. It only leaves your iPhone if you choose to turn on backup, in which case it’s encrypted and linked only to you.

analytics.title: Never in analytics
analytics.body: Your period dates, flow, symptoms, moods, sex, tests and pregnancy logs are never included in analytics, logs or crash reports.
analytics.detail: Your private entries are used by Mochi on your iPhone to support the features you choose to use.

backup.title: Backup and sync
backup.body: Backup is optional. If you choose to turn it on, your backup is encrypted, stored in the EU and linked only to you.
backup.detail: You can use Mochi’s core features offline and without an account. Your cycle data stays on your iPhone unless you choose backup.

subscriptions.title: Subscriptions
subscriptions.body: Mochi Plus is an optional subscription. You can keep using the free core features without subscribing.
subscriptions.detail: App Store purchases and subscription management are handled through Apple. A subscription does not change how Mochi keeps your cycle entries private.

rights.title: You stay in control
rights.body: You decide what information to add to Mochi. All core features work without creating an account or enabling backup.
rights.detail: If you have questions about your information or want help with a privacy request, contact us using the details below.

children.title: Children’s privacy
children.body: The same privacy approach applies to cycle entries: they stay on the iPhone unless optional backup is enabled.
children.detail: If you are a parent or guardian with a question about privacy, please contact us. Avoid including sensitive health information in your message.

contact.title: Let’s talk about privacy
contact.body: Questions about this policy or how Mochi handles your information? We’re here to help.
contact.detail: Please avoid including period dates, symptoms or other health information in your message.

using.title: Using Mochi
using.body: Mochi is a period tracking app for iPhone that helps you log your cycle, symptoms, moods and more, get predictions and set helpful reminders (such as a pad change reminder), and collect cute flavors through daily check-ins.
using.detail: By using Mochi, you agree to these Terms of Use. If you don’t agree with them, please don’t use the app.

health.title: Health disclaimer
health.body: Mochi is for general wellness and cycle tracking only. It is not a medical device and does not provide medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Always contact a qualified healthcare professional if you have any health concerns or questions about your cycle.
health.detail: Mochi can help you spot patterns and estimate your next period, fertile window and ovulation day based on the information you log, but these are estimates and may not be accurate for everyone.

subscriptions.title: Mochi Plus subscriptions
subscriptions.body: Mochi Plus is optional. Before you subscribe, the App Store purchase screen shows the price, billing period and any offer that applies. Apple handles payment through your Apple Account.
subscriptions.detail: Recurring subscriptions renew until canceled. Manage or cancel yours in iPhone Settings > your name > Subscriptions. Deleting Mochi does not cancel a subscription.

content.title: Your content
content.body: The cycle entries, symptoms, moods and other information you log are yours. You keep ownership of your content when you use Mochi.
content.detail: Our privacy policy explains how your information is handled, including optional backup. Please keep your device and any account you use secure.

acceptable-use.title: Acceptable use
acceptable-use.body: Use Mochi for your own personal cycle tracking and in accordance with applicable law. Please use the app and its features responsibly.
acceptable-use.detail: Do not misuse or disrupt the app, try to bypass its security, or access someone else’s information without their permission.

changes.detail: Please review the terms when the app changes. Nothing in these terms takes away rights you have under applicable consumer law.

editorial.title: Our editorial approach
editorial.description: Who publishes the Mochi blog, how we use sources, and how to report a correction.
editorial.intro: Mochi publishes this blog to help people understand period tracking and make informed choices about the tools they use. The same company makes the Mochi app mentioned in our articles.

publisher.title: Who writes the articles
publisher.body: Articles are attributed to Mochi as the publisher. We do not present this byline as a medical qualification or claim independent testing of our own app. We do not currently have a clinician reviewing these articles.

sources.title: How we use sources
sources.body: Basic health information links to sources such as the NHS and the US Office on Women's Health. Product and privacy descriptions link to the relevant official documentation. Each article includes its sources so you can read the underlying guidance.

editing.title: How the copy is prepared
editing.body: These launch articles were drafted with AI assistance, edited for clear language, and checked against the cited sources. An editorial check is not a clinical review. Illustrations are AI-generated artwork and do not show a medical result or a verified app screen.

limits.title: What the articles can help with
limits.body: The blog covers basic tracking habits, product features, and privacy questions. It does not provide personal medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, or contraception guidance. Contact a qualified healthcare professional about health concerns.

dates.title: Publication dates and updates
dates.body: Publication dates identify when an article was first added. An updated date is shown only when its content changes substantively. Rebuilding the website does not refresh article dates.

corrections.title: Corrections and questions
corrections.body: If you find a factual error, send the article URL and the passage you want us to check. Please avoid including period dates, symptoms, or other sensitive health information in your message.

bestWay.question: What is the best way to track my period?
bestWay.answer: Choose a method you can use consistently: a period app, calendar, or notebook. Record when bleeding starts and ends, its heaviness, and any symptoms you want to follow. Reviewing your entries can help you notice patterns and changes.

meaning.question: What does “tracking period” mean?
meaning.answer: Period tracking means recording your bleeding dates and related symptoms over time. Day 1 is the first day of your period. Cycle length is counted from that day to the day before your next period starts.

noBleeding.question: How do I track my menstrual cycle if I don't bleed?
noBleeding.answer: You can keep a dated symptom and mood diary, but symptoms alone cannot reliably confirm ovulation or your cycle phase. Some hormonal contraception changes bleeding and ovulation. If pregnancy is possible, take a pregnancy test. Seek medical advice if you miss three periods in a row, or sooner if you are concerned.

whenToStart.question: When should you start tracking your period?
whenToStart.answer: You can start recording periods from your first one, or at any later time. Begin with the bleeding dates you know and keep adding entries. If you start midway through a cycle, leave uncertain dates blank instead of guessing.
